record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Let F be the free group of finite rank ≥ 2. Does there exist a finite subset S ⊂ F such that there is a unique total order on F under which all elements from S are positive?

evidence.quote: 3.25∗ . (S. H. McCleary [83] Problem 12.51) Let F be the free group of finite rank ≥ 2. Does there exist a finite subset S ⊂ F such that there is a unique total order on F under which all elements from S are positive?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a free group of finite rank $n \geq 2$. A total order $\leq$ on $F$ is called bi-invariant (a total group order) if for all $a,b,c,d \in F$, $a \leq b$ implies $cad \leq cbd$; equivalently, the set $P = \{g \in F : g > 1\}$ (the positive cone) satisfies $P \cdot P \subseteq P$, $F = P \sqcup \{1\} \sqcup P^{-1}$, and $gPg^{-1} = P$ for all $g \in F$.

Does there exist a finite subset $S \subset F$ such that there is exactly one total (bi-invariant) order on $F$ under which every element of $S$ is positive?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (attributed to S. H. McCleary, Kourovka Notebook Problem 12.51) is listed in the compilation of unsolved problems on ordered and orderable groups and is marked with an asterisk indicating open status. Recent literature on orders of free groups (e.g., uncountable families of left orders, non-regularity of positive cones in free products) does not report a resolution of this uniqueness question, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: No positive cone in a free product is regular
status_evidence.snippet: For free products of nontrivial finitely generated orderable groups, no positive cone satisfies certain regularity conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on free group/free product orders does not resolve uniqueness from finite positive sets.
